title: Prevent RSV lower respiratory tract disease in older adults through vaccination

concept.text: Prevent clinically important RSV respiratory disease in older adults using active immunization. This achieved target is distinct from infant monoclonal-antibody prophylaxis and from universal respiratory vaccines. Proposed completion test: FDA vaccine licensure for adults aged at least 60 years, supported by a randomized trial of more than 20,000 participants showing efficacy against laboratory-confirmed RSV lower respiratory tract disease during the first season. Test set by: FDA; the Arexvy clinical programme and regulatory review supply the population and endpoint. Reported achieved: FDA approved Arexvy on 3 May 2023. Overlaps: VIR-04. Sources given: [FDA first RSV vaccine announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-respiratory-syncytial-virus-rsv-vaccine) ; [FDA Arexvy regulatory assessment](https://www.fda.gov/media/168519/download).

page.title: RSV vaccines against lower respiratory tract disease in older adults
page.definition: Vaccination reduces laboratory-confirmed lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD), which affects the lungs and lower airways, caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in adults aged 60 years or older.

goal.need: Before vaccination, RSV accounted for an estimated 60,000–160,000 hospitalizations and 6,000–10,000 deaths each year among US adults aged 65 or older. Routine care relieves symptoms after illness begins. In a Danish trial of adults aged 60 or older, 1 of 65,642 assigned the bivalent vaccine and 12 of 65,634 assigned no vaccine were hospitalized for RSV lower respiratory tract disease during winter 2024–25. The expected benefit is greatest at age 75 or older and in people with risk factors such as chronic heart or lung disease.

completion.title: FDA licenses a vaccine against RSV lower respiratory tract disease in adults aged ≥60 years.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a biologics license application for at least one vaccine whose indication covers active immunization of adults aged 60 years or older to prevent lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, biologics licensure and the Arexvy indication in the May 23, 2023 replacement approval letter, effective May 3, 2023.
completion.threshold_quote: prevention of lower respiratory tract disease caused by respiratory syncytial virus in individuals 60 years of age and older.
completion.basis: Arexvy was the first vaccine to meet this test, effective May 3, 2023. FDA subsequently licensed Abrysvo and mResvia for the same older-adult indication. The 20% lower confidence bound belongs to the Arexvy efficacy protocol. FDA’s licensing decision also takes safety and manufacturing quality into account.

milestones.title: An investigational new drug application takes effect for human testing of an RSV vaccine.
milestones.criterion: The sponsor submits the laboratory, animal and product-quality evidence for its RSV vaccine to FDA in an investigational new drug application. The application takes effect 30 days after FDA receives it unless FDA places the investigation on clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40(b).
milestones.threshold_quote: Thirty days after FDA receives the IND, unless FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigations described in the IND are subject to a clinical hold

milestones.title: Independent safety reviews permit the RSVPreF3 phase 1/2 trial to proceed in adults aged 60–80.
milestones.criterion: In NCT03814590, a favorable independent safety review after dose 1 in adults aged 18–40 permits enrollment of the first adults aged 60–80. Favorable second and third reviews permit expansion to the remaining older adults. A favorable fourth review permits their second dose, after the committee examines safety data through day 7 after dose 2 in the initial older cohort and through day 7 after dose 1 in participants vaccinated by the review date.
milestones.set_by: GlaxoSmithKline Biologicals SA, NCT03814590, protocol amendment 1, section 7.10.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: If this fourth IDMC evaluation outcome is favorable, the study participants enrolled in Step 2 will be administered the second vaccine dose.

milestones.title: In AReSVi-006, the lower confidence bound for efficacy against first-season RSV LRTD exceeds 20%.
milestones.criterion: In adults aged 60 or older, compare one dose of RSVPreF3 with placebo for the first externally adjudicated episode of RT-PCR-confirmed RSV LRTD from day 15 in the first RSV season. The lower limit of the two-sided confidence interval for efficacy must exceed 20%, using a 96.95% interval at the interim analysis. LRTD requires at least two lower respiratory symptoms or signs, including at least one sign, or at least three lower respiratory symptoms, lasting at least 24 hours.
milestones.set_by: GlaxoSmithKline Biologicals SA, AReSVi-006 protocol NCT04886596, primary efficacy objective.
milestones.threshold_quote: The lower limit (LL) of the 2-sided confidence interval (CI) for vaccine efficacy (VE) is above 20%.

milestones.title: FDA’s review committee recommends licensing an RSV vaccine to prevent LRTD in adults aged ≥60.
milestones.criterion: FDA’s multidisciplinary biologics license application review committee recommends approval for active immunization against RSV lower respiratory tract disease in adults aged 60 or older after assessing the clinical, nonclinical and manufacturing evidence and the balance of benefits and risks.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Arexvy Summary Basis for Regulatory Action, recommended regulatory action and benefit/risk assessment.
milestones.threshold_quote: The Review Committee recommends approval of this product.

milestones.title: An RSV vaccine candidate elicits a functional immune response in nonclinical testing.
milestones.criterion: Nonclinical testing demonstrates a functional antibody response, a cell-mediated response, or both after vaccination, using a measure appropriate to the candidate and its route of administration. For a protein vaccine, serum antibodies that neutralize RSV provide one such measure.
milestones.set_by: European Medicines Agency, guideline on clinical evaluation of RSV products, section 4.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: a functional humoral and/or cell-mediated immune response can be achieved post-vaccination

milestones.title: Safety and immune responses in adults aged 60–80 support selection of an RSVPreF3 formulation.
milestones.criterion: Select a formulation for further development from the nine tested in adults aged 60–80. Assess safety, reactions after vaccination and immune responses. The protocol gives primary weight among immune measures to RSV-A neutralizing antibody titers and the CD4+ T-cell response.
milestones.set_by: GlaxoSmithKline Biologicals SA, NCT03814590, protocol amendment 1, section 1.2.2.
milestones.threshold_quote: select a formulation for further development of the RSV vaccine.

not_found: No universal numerical preclinical or phase 1/2 pass threshold was found in FDA development guidance or the published RSVPreF3 phase 1/2 report.
The public FDA summary does not disclose rabbit sample sizes for the two repeat-dose toxicity studies.

results.finding: The RSVPreF3 IND was submitted on October 19, 2018.
results.detail: The later Fast Track designation is a separate regulatory action.

results.finding: Study 002 selected 120 µg RSVPreF3 with AS01E for phase 3. The reported older-adult arms included 100 formulation and 101 placebo recipients.
results.detail: The two reported arm sizes cover the selected formulation and placebo.
results.quote:
The safety and immunogenicity data provided in this study 
supported selection of 120 μg RSVPreF3 with AS01E administered as a single dose 
for further evaluation in the Phase 3 studies.

results.finding: In AReSVi-006 (n=24,960), the first-season RSV LRTD efficacy lower confidence bound was 57.9%.
results.quote:
The case split was 7 cases in the RSVPreF3-AS01E group 
compared to 40 cases in the placebo group with a VE of 82.6% (96.95% CI 57.9, 
94.1).

results.finding: FDA’s BLA review committee recommended AREXVY approval to prevent RSV LRTD in adults aged 60 or older.
results.quote:
the Review Committee recommends approval of
AREXVY for the labeled indication and usage.

results.finding: NCT03814590 enrolled 1,005 adults aged 60–80, of whom 970 received both doses under independent safety oversight.
results.detail: The main text refers readers to supplementary information for the review schedule and reports the committee's safety finding in aggregate.
results.quote:
IDMC evaluations identified no safety concerns precluding use 
of any vaccine formulation throughout the study.

results.finding: Among nine RSVPreF3 formulations tested in 1,005 adults aged 60–80, the 120 μg AS01E formulation was selected for further development.
results.detail: The formulation advanced as a single-dose schedule. The second dose did not raise RSV-A neutralizing titers or polyfunctional CD4+ T-cell frequencies above their post-dose-1 peaks.
results.quote:
Based on safety and immunogenicity profiles, the AS01E-adjuvanted vaccine containing 120 μg of RSVPreF3 was 
selected for further clinical development.

results.finding: AReSVi-006 RSVPreF3 OA vs. placebo (n=24,960) had a 57.9% lower confidence bound for first-season RSV LRTD efficacy.
results.detail: Median follow-up was 6.7 months. All adjudicated RSV LRTD cases occurred in the Northern Hemisphere.
results.quote:
The vaccine efficacy was 
82.6% (96.95% confidence interval [CI], 57.9 to 
94.1) (Table 2); thus, the primary objective was 
met (lower limit of confidence interval, >20%).

results.finding: FDA licensed AREXVY to prevent RSV lower respiratory tract disease in adults aged ≥60. Sample size is inapplicable to this licensing decision.
results.detail: The May 23, 2023 replacement letter corrected the adjuvant component’s dating period and retained May 3, 2023 as the effective approval date.
results.quote:
Respiratory 
Syncytial Virus Vaccine, Adjuvanted is indicated for active immunization for the 
prevention of lower respiratory tract disease caused by respiratory syncytial virus in 
individuals 60 years of age and older.

results.finding: RV-1770 elicited neutralization against 2 RSV types in cotton rats. Animal count unreported.
results.quote:
It demonstrated immunogenic responses and neutralization 
against both type A and B strains of RSV in preclinical cotton rat studies.

results.finding: FDA cleared the RV-1770 RSV vaccine IND in December 2023. The Phase I trial planned to enroll 162 adults.
results.quote:

from the U.S. FDA to commence a Phase I clinical trial for RV-1770, an mRNA vaccine 
targeting the human RSV.

results.finding: RSV-naive mice given RSVPreF3/AS01 (n=35 across three groups) had post-dose-3 serum RSV-A/B neutralization geometric mean titers of 4,527–8,261 ED60.
results.detail: The three injections were given two weeks apart. Neutralization titers were significantly higher in each AS01 group than in the unadjuvanted vaccine group at both measured time points.
results.quote: In the three AS01 groups, the RSV-A/B-specific geometric mean neutralization titers (neutralization GMTs) detected after the second dose were increased after the third dose (D28 and D42 neutralization GMTs across AS01 groups: 659–1368 and 4527–8261 ED60, respectively).
